prompt:
Approach this as a Economist / Game Theorist. Sees resource allocation, equilibria, mechanism design, and incentive structures. Bring that lens to the problem.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Hysteresis and bistability test (path-dependence of equilibrium)
ideas.description: Expose cells to graded doses of a transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., PMA, stress, or optogenetic c-Fos/c-Jun), then measure AP-1 target accessibility and expression after washout. Hysteresis, bimodal single-cell distributions, and a persistent high state at identical final conditions would indicate multiple stable equilibria, the game-theoretic signature of memory rather than a transient response.

ideas.title: Time-resolved ATAC/CUT&Tag with AP-1 occupancy through stimulus and washout
ideas.description: Track chromatin accessibility, AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding, and histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) at defined time points after a stimulus ends. Test whether AP-1 sites stay open and primed (a 'committed investment' in regulatory state) and whether the memory-bearing loci are enriched for AP-1 motifs relative to matched controls.

ideas.title: Necessity/sufficiency via acute degradation and optogenetic timing (mechanism-design intervention)
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative AP-1 (A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either during priming, during the memory interval, or at re-challenge, and optogenetically pulse it in naive cells. If depletion only during priming erases memory while depletion during the interval or re-challenge has different effects, you can separate AP-1 as the writer, the maintainer, or the reader of memory.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation response assay with single-cell readouts (primed vs. naive payoff)
ideas.description: Apply a first and second stimulus separated by variable delays, and measure the speed, amplitude, and cell-to-cell variability of transcriptional response (scRNA-seq, live reporters) versus naive cells. Fit decay kinetics of the primed advantage to estimate memory half-life, and test whether it depends on AP-1 dosage or motif integrity.

ideas.title: Motif-level perturbation and feedback-loop modeling
ideas.description: Edit AP-1 motifs at candidate enhancers with CRISPR base editing, or run a massively parallel reporter assay, to test whether memory is locus-intrinsic. In parallel, build a dynamical model with AP-1 positive autoregulation (c-Jun autoinduction) and chromatin feedback, fit it to the data, and test whether it predicts when memory is stable, using inhibition of feedback components as the falsification step.
